blocks.text: Introduction

Assalam o alaikum! Unit 5 ka mauzu hai Partial Fractions (juzvi kasoor, yani ek fraction ke chhote chhote hisse). Is sabaq mein hum yeh samjhenge ke yeh unit kis cheez ke baare mein hai, equation aur identity mein kya farq hai, aur rational fraction kise kehte hain. Yeh sab buniyaadi baatein hain; aage ka poora unit inhi par khara hai, is liye inhein aaram se samajh lijiye.
Pichli classes mein aap ne seekha tha ke do ya zyada rational fractions ko jama kar ke ek single rational fraction kaise banate hain. Misaal ke taur par:

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yeh (i) jama kaise hua? Bilkul aam fractions ki tarah. Pehle common denominator (mushtarka nasab) lete hain: \((x-1)(x+2)\). Phir har numerator ko us factor se multiply karte hain jo uske apne denominator mein kam hai:
\[1(x+2) + 2(x-1)\]
\[= x + 2 + 2x - 2 = 3x\]
(ii) mein common denominator \((x+1)^{2}(x-2)\) hai, aur numerator yeh banta hai:
\[2(x+1)(x-2) + (x-2) + 3(x+1)^{2}\]
\[= 5x^{2} + 5x - 3\]
Khud check kijiye: \(2(x+1)(x-2) = 2x^{2} - 2x - 4\), aur \(3(x+1)^{2} = 3x^{2} + 6x + 3\). In sab ko \((x - 2)\) ke saath jama karein to \(5x^{2} + 5x - 3\) milta hai.
Jama karna aasan kaam hai. Is unit ka asal sawal ulta hai: agar humein sirf right-hand side di jaye, to left-hand side ke hisse kaise dhoondein?

Is unit mein hum (i) aur (ii) ki tarteeb ko ulta karna seekhenge, yani ek single rational function ko do ya zyada simple rational functions ke sum ki shakal mein likhna. Yeh chhote hisse Partial Fractions kehlaate hain.

Kisi rational function ko partial fractions ke sum ki shakal mein likhne ke amal ko Partial Fraction Resolution (juzvi kasoor mein torna) kehte hain. Calculus mein yeh bohat qeemti auzaar hai, kyun ke is se ek mushkil rational function ko simple fractions ke sum mein toda ja sakta hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Arithmetic se misaal lijiye: \(\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{3} = \frac{5}{6}\). Jama karna aage chalna hai. Partial fractions peeche chalna hai: \(\frac{5}{6}\) se shuru kar ke \(\frac{1}{2}\) aur \(\frac{1}{3}\) wapas dhoondna.
Socho jaise doodh patti chai bana li; ab chai se doodh, patti aur cheeni alag karni hai. Fractions mein yeh kaam mumkin hai, aur is unit mein hum iska tareeqa seekhenge.
Peeche kyun chalein? Ek ulajhi hui single fraction jaise \(\frac{3x}{(x-1)(x+2)}\) ke saath kaam karna mushkil hai, lekin uske hisse \(\frac{1}{x-1}\) aur \(\frac{2}{x+2}\) bohat simple hain. Agli classes mein calculus (integration) aur series ke sums mein aap har simple hisse ko alag alag handle karenge, jo kahin zyada aasan hai. Is liye yeh unit aage chal kar bohat kaam aata hai.

Ab ek zaroori farq samajhte hain jo aage har sawal mein kaam aayega: equation aur identity ka farq. Pehli nazar mein dono mein '=' ka nishaan hota hai, is liye dono ek jaisi lagti hain, lekin dono ka kirdar bilkul alag hai. Ek sirf kuch values par sach hoti hai, doosri har value par.
Barabri ke nishaan '=' ko istemal kar ke banaya gaya open sentence (khula jumla, jis mein variable ho) equation kehlata hai. Equations ki do qismein hain:
Conditional equation: yeh aisi equation hai jis mein do algebraic expressions sirf variable ki kuch khaas values ke liye barabar hoti hain, misaal ke taur par:

items: (a) \(2x = 3\) ek conditional equation hai aur yeh sirf tab sach hai jab \(x = \frac{3}{2}\) ho.
(b) \(x^{2} + x - 6 = 0\) ek conditional equation hai aur yeh sirf \(x = 2, -3\) ke liye sach hai.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.text: Aasani ke liye conditional equation ko sirf equation kaha jata hai.
Identity: yeh aisi equation hai jo variable ki har value ke liye sach rehti hai, misaal ke taur par:

items: (a) \((a + b)x \equiv ax + bx\) ek identity hai aur iski dono sides \(x\) ki har value ke liye barabar hain.
(b) \((x + 3)(x + 4) \equiv x^{2} + 7x + 12\) bhi ek identity hai jo \(x\) ki har value ke liye sach hai.

blocks.text: Aasani ke liye nishaan "=" hum equation aur identity dono ke liye istemal karenge.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Nishaan \(\equiv\) ko "identically equal to" (har haal mein barabar) parha jata hai.
Dono qismon mein farq kaise pehchaanein? Seedha tareeqa: \(x\) ki do teen values rakh kar dekhiye.
Conditional equation (b) mein \(x = 0\) rakhein to \(0 + 0 - 6 = -6\) aata hai, jo \(0\) nahin. Yani yahan equation jhooti ho gayi, is liye yeh sirf conditional hai; yeh sirf \(2\) aur \(-3\) par sach hai.
Identity (b) mein \(x = 0\) rakhein to \(12 = 12\), aur \(x = 1\) rakhein to \(4 \times 5 = 20\) aur \(1 + 7 + 12 = 20\). Har dafa sach! Kyun? Kyun ke left side ko multiply kar ke kholein to bilkul right side ban jati hai: \(x^{2} + 4x + 3x + 12 = x^{2} + 7x + 12\).
Yeh farq is poore unit ki chaabi hai: ek rational fraction aur uske partial fractions aapas mein identity ke taur par barabar hote hain. Is liye humein ijazat hai ke us mein \(x\) ki koi bhi aasan value rakh dein. Isi azaadi se 5.1.3 mein numerators ki unknown values nikalti hain.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
Neeche diye gaye jumlon mein se kaun identity hai aur kaun conditional equation?
1. \(x + x = 2x\)
2. \(x + 5 = 9\)
3. \((x - 1)^{2} = x^{2} - 2x + 1\)
Jawab: 1 aur 3 identities hain (har \(x\) par sach, kyun ke left side khol kar right side ban jati hai); 2 conditional hai, sirf \(x = 4\) par sach.

blocks.title: Dhyan dein
blocks.text: Kitab aage chal kar \(\equiv\) ki jagah aam taur par \(=\) hi likhti hai ("for convenience"). Is liye jab aap partial fractions wale sawalon mein \(=\) dekhein to yaad rakhiye ke wahan asal mein identity hai, conditional equation nahin. Yahi wajah hai ke hum wahan \(x\) ki koi bhi aasan value (jaise woh value jo kisi factor ko zero kar de) rakh sakte hain. Agar yeh baat zehan mein na rahe to students sochte hain ke "\(x\) ki value to sawal mein di hi nahin, main kaise rakh doon?" Jawab yeh hai: identity har value par sach hai, is liye rakhna bilkul jaaiz hai.
5.1 Rational Fraction

Aisa expression jo \(\frac{P(x)}{Q(x)}\) ki shakal mein ho, jahan \(P(x)\) aur \(Q(x)\) \(x\) mein polynomials hon jin ke coefficients real numbers hon, aur \(Q(x) \ne 0\) ho, rational fraction kehlata hai. Rational fraction ki do qismein hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Pehle yeh yaad kar lein ke polynomial kya hai. \(x\) mein polynomial aise terms ka sum hai jaise \(5x^{3}\), \(-2x\), \(7\), jin mein \(x\) ki powers poore (whole) numbers \(0, 1, 2, \ldots\) hon. Polynomial ki degree (darja) us mein \(x\) ki sab se bari power hoti hai: \(2x^{3} - x + 4\) ki degree 3, \(x - 2\) ki degree 1, aur kisi non-zero constant jaise \(7\) ki degree 0 hai (kyun ke \(7 = 7x^{0}\)).
Is liye \(\frac{x+1}{x^{2}-4}\) rational fraction hai, lekin \(\frac{\sqrt{x}+1}{x-4}\) nahin, kyun ke \(\sqrt{x} = x^{1/2}\) mein power poora number nahin.
\(Q(x) \ne 0\) ki shart kyun? Kyun ke zero se divide karne ka koi matlab nahin hota; denominator zero ho jaye to fraction hi bekaar ho jati hai.
Dono qismon ke naam bilkul arithmetic ki fractions jaise hain: \(\frac{3}{4}\) proper hai (upar wala number neeche wale se chhota) aur \(\frac{7}{4}\) improper. Rational fractions mein "chhota" ka matlab hai degree mein chhota. Yahi do qismein agle do pages par hain: 5.1.1 aur 5.1.2.

blocks.title: About this unit
blocks.text:
Unit 5 ka raasta: 5.1.1 proper aur 5.1.2 improper rational fractions (saath mein barabar polynomials wala theorem), phir 5.1.3 mein resolution ka tareeqa chaar cases mein: non-repeated linear factors, repeated linear factors (Exercise 5.1), non-repeated irreducible quadratic factors aur repeated irreducible quadratic factors (Exercise 5.2).
Pichli classes ki jo cheezein chahiyein: polynomials ko factorize karna, polynomials ki long division, aur simple simultaneous equations hal karna. In mein se koi kamzor ho to pehle use dohra lijiye; is unit mein yeh baar baar aayengi.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Yeh hamari taraf se ek chhoti si misaal hai (kitab ka sawal nahin), taa ke "ulta chalna" mehsoos ho:
\[\dfrac{1}{x+1} - \dfrac{1}{x+2}\]
\[= \dfrac{(x+2) - (x+1)}{(x+1)(x+2)} = \dfrac{1}{(x+1)(x+2)}\]
Yani agar koi poochhe ke \(\frac{1}{(x+1)(x+2)}\) ke partial fractions kya hain, to jawab hai \(\frac{1}{x+1} - \frac{1}{x+2}\). Yeh jawab hum ne andaze se nahin, ulti tarteeb se dekha. 5.1.3 mein hum yeh kaam bina andaze ke, ek pakke tareeqe se karna seekhenge.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Partial fractions rational fractions ke jama karne ka ulta amal hai: ek fraction ko simple fractions ke sum mein likhna.
2. Rational function ko partial fractions ke sum mein likhna partial fraction resolution kehlata hai.
3. Conditional equation sirf kuch khaas values par sach hoti hai; identity (\(\equiv\)) har value par sach hoti hai.
4. Partial fractions ka jawab identity hota hai, is liye us mein \(x\) ki koi bhi value rakh sakte hain.
5. Rational fraction \(\frac{P(x)}{Q(x)}\) hai jahan \(P(x)\), \(Q(x)\) polynomials hain aur \(Q(x) \ne 0\); yeh proper ya improper hoti hai.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Identity ko "solve" karne ki koshish karna: identity ka koi khaas hal nahin hota, har \(x\) us par poora utarta hai.
2. Har us fraction ko rational fraction keh dena jis mein \(x\) ho: numerator aur denominator dono polynomials hone chahiyein (\(\sqrt{x}\) ya \(\frac{1}{x}\) andar nahin).
3. \(\frac{1}{x-1} + \frac{2}{x+2}\) ko \(\frac{3}{2x+1}\) likh dena: numerators aur denominators alag alag kabhi jama nahin hote. Hamesha common denominator lein, jaise \(\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{3}\) kabhi \(\frac{2}{5}\) nahin hota.
